one_month_reasoning: Effective start is the $64.85 after-hours price (-5.6% vs the $68.69 close) after the Q3 print: EPS beat ($0.87 vs $0.82) but the 2026 ad revenue outlook was cut to ~$2.7B from ~$3B, revenue landed at the low end ($51.1B) and FCF guidance fell to ~$12B. No earnings or guidance event falls inside the window to 2026-11-19. Scheduled items: analyst target revisions this week, Nielsen's US Gauge releases (alt-data that has shown YouTube gaining share; a headline weak Netflix month would weigh), and the Thanksgiving-Eve NFL game (Nov 25) falls just after the window. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: post-earnings drift after a negative guidance reaction and weak momentum (-43% over 12 months, Wells Fargo/HSBC downgrades in September) versus reversal from a fresh 52-week low with a $22.3B buyback authorisation being used aggressively ($4.8B in Q3). No new event in the window from round 2: the Paramount-WBD merger already closed on 2026-10-06 (priced before the print), and its integration plans are a slow-moving risk, not a November catalyst. Net: centre slightly below the after-hours price (~$64.5) with monthly vol ~11% (37%/3.5), a near-symmetric spread; P(>= $68.69, the pre-print close) ~27%.

fair_value.method: Engine blend at the 2027-10-20 horizon: segment-driven DCF $69.71 (w 0.20; WACC 9.2% on a 5.12% risk-free, g 3%, GAAP EBIT margin 31.5% to 36.0%, tax 15.5%), 18.0x NTM GAAP P/E $75.98 (w 0.70) and 14.0x NTM EV/EBITDA $71.22 (w 0.10), less a $0.8B probability-weighted M&A adjustment = $74.25, +14.5% vs the $64.85 after-hours price.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Segment build: UCAN subscription $18.96B (+10%,+7%,+5.5%,+5%,+4%), international subscription $24.72B (+11.4%,+10%,+9%,+8%,+7%), advertising $1.5B (+80%,+44%,+30%,+22%,+15%) => revenue $51.1B FY2026, $56.5B FY2027 (+10.6%), ~$70.8B FY2030; GAAP EBIT margin 31.5/33.3/34.5/35.5/36.0%; tax 15.5%; content cash gap 30% of incremental revenue; capex 2.7% then 1.8%; WACC 9.2% (rf 5.12%, beta 1.03, ERP 4.20%); Gordon g 3.0%; net debt $7.1B now, $7.5B at horizon; shares 4,195M -3%/yr; M&A adjustment -$0.8B.

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-K revenue FY2025.

inputs_detail.input: FY2025 revenue by segment: UCAN subscription $18,960M; international subscription $24,723M; advertising $1,500M
inputs_detail.derivation: Regional FY2025 revenue in the 10-K and the Q4 2025 letter (sum of quarters): UCAN ~$19.96B, EMEA ~$14.52B, LATAM ~$5.36B, APAC ~$5.35B (sum ~45.19B). Advertising 'over $1.5B' in 2025 (Omdia figure in source 13; Netflix stated the same in its Q4'25 letter). Ads split by judgment ~2/3 UCAN ($1.0B) and ~1/3 international ($0.5B) because the ad tier launched first and is deepest in the US; UCAN sub = 19,960-1,000 = 18,960; intl sub = 45,183-19,960-500 = 24,723; 18,960+24,723+1,500 = 45,183.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If US ads were ~80% of the total, UCAN subscription would be ~$0.2B smaller and international ~$0.2B larger: no material value effect because both carry the same margin.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 letter full-year 2026 revenue outlook $51.1B (13% growth). Split: ads ~$2.7B (letter), remainder $48.4B = +10.8% on $43,683M subscription base; UCAN subscription +10% (US price rise March 2026), international +11.4% (balancing).
Letter: ad revenue now ~$2.7B vs ~$3B prior; call: ads growing 'over 80% this year'. 2.7/1.5 = 1.8x.

Ad tier enters 15 new countries in 2027 (letter); WARC forecasts Netflix's share of global CTV ad spend rising from 3.7% (2025) to 9.2% (2027) (source 13). We haircut the earlier street/industry 2027 view because management is 'behind our aggressive target' and cut 2026 by $0.3B: $2.7B x 1.44 = $3.9B.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Bull reading (ad-tier ARM gap closes, 250M+ ad-tier reach): ~$4.5B, +$0.6B revenue, ~+$1.5/share at 18x after tax. Bear: $3.3B, -$1.5/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Fades from +44% toward market growth; 2030 ads ~$7.1B vs the $8B 2030 target cited from Omdia in source 13 (we sit ~11% below to reflect the 2026 shortfall).
inputs_detail.variant_view: At the Omdia $8B 2030 path, +$0.9B revenue in 2030, ~+$2/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 +10% follows the March 2026 price rise and the $51.1B FY2026 guide (letter). FY2027 cut to +7% from +8% in round 1 because the price step laps and a larger direct US rival now exists: WBD's merger with Paramount Skydance completed on 2026-10-06 (WBD S-8 POS), and the two services (Paramount+ 79M, HBO Max 128M; ~200M combined) are to be merged into one platform (PPC Land). Then +5.5/+5/+4 as US TV-time share is flat to down (Nielsen: Netflix 7.9% June 2026 vs 8.3%; YouTube 14.2% July). CFO: 'sustain double-digit revenue growth' in 2027 (call); total FY2027 growth in this set is +10.6%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If YouTube and the combined Paramount-WBD erode pricing power (Wells Fargo: per-member hours ~8% below 2023), UCAN could grow 3-4%: bear scenario (-3pt on all segments).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3'26 F/X-neutral growth: EMEA +9%, LATAM +12%, APAC +15%; India revenue ~+18-20% and view hours +24% (letter, call). Nielsen Poland: Netflix TV share 1.7% to 1.9% Jul-Aug 2026 (source 11) shows international engagement still rising. Fade ~1pt a year.

inputs_detail.input: Operating (EBIT) margin, GAAP after SBC: FY2026 31.5%, FY2027 33.3%, FY2028 34.5%, FY2029 35.5%, FY2030 36.0%
inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 31.5% guided (Q3 letter); it carries ~$275M of WBD acquisition costs (Q4'25 letter, ~0.5pt) and the Q4 layoff charge (~1.2pt of Q4, ~0.3pt of the year), so underlying ~32.3%. FY2027 33.3% = underlying +1pt (CFO: 'we look to expand margins'; savings not quantified). History: FY2025 13,326.6/45,183 = 29.5% (F10/F3), TTM 29.7% (F13/F6). Trimmed from round 1 (37.5% FY2030) after the supervisor asked for a scaled-peer argument: 36.0% FY2030 sits between a content-heavy media floor and an ad platform ceiling. inputs_detail.variant_view: Bull: 38-40% by 2030 (Netflix added ~2-3pt a year 2023-2025), ~+$4/share. Bear: margin stalls ~33% (sports rights, Paramount-WBD bidding): bear scenario -2.5pt.

Beta: own weekly log-return regression of NFLX on SPY (Yahoo): 0.92 over 2y, 1.04 over 3y (Blume 1.03), 1.43 over 5y (dominated by the 2022 collapse); 1.03 used. ERP 4.20% = Damodaran implied ERP on 2026-10-01 (round 1 used a 5.0% judgment). Cost of debt: TTM interest 847.5 / debt 14,309.3 = 5.92% (F74/F96), after 15.5% tax 5.00%. Weights: equity 4,163.9M x $64.85 = $270.0B (F95), debt $14.3B => 95%/5%. WACC = 0.95 x 9.45% + 0.05 x 5.00% = 8.98% + 0.25% = 9.22%, rounded to 9.2%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: With the 5y Blume beta 1.29, CoE 10.5% and WACC ~10.2%: DCF ~-$10/share, fair value ~-$2 (DCF weight 0.2).

bear.story: Engagement keeps sliding to YouTube/creator video (Nielsen share 8.3% to 7.9% in a year) and the newly closed Paramount-WBD combination (HBO Max + Paramount+, ~200M subs) bids up content and pulls licensed titles; price rises meet churn, subscription growth falls toward 5%, ads stall near $3.3B in 2027, margin stalls ~33%, and the market pays ~14x P/E. Engine: growth -3pt, margin -2.5pt, multiple -4 turns, WACC +0.5pt.

base.story: Revenue +10.6% in 2027 (ads ~$3.9B with 15 new ad markets), margin +1.8pt as acquisition and layoff costs lap, EPS ~$3.8 in line with consensus; the engagement debate stays open, so the stock holds ~18x NTM P/E.

bull.story: Live sports (NFL, Women's World Cup), ad-tech catch-up and pricing reaccelerate growth; the first annual engagement report shows per-member hours stabilising and Gauge share turning up; rerates to ~21x. Engine: growth +2pt, margin +1.5pt, multiple +3 turns.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E 6.3x (CMCSA) to 119.1x (LYV); median 22.2x across 11 table names. Core set ex LYV, TTWO, ROKU, CMCSA (non-comparable earnings bases or businesses) and ex GOOGL (FY2026 EPS inflated by stake gains): FOXA 11.1, DIS 15.2, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4 => median 20.4x. EV/EBITDA NTM is not available in the run table; TTM median 13.9x (range 4.8x-27.7x, 6 names).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18.0x NTM P/E: inside the range, ~12% below the core median (20.4x) and ~19% below the 11-name median (22.2x); below META (22.2x), above DIS (15.2x). 14.0x EV/EBITDA at the TTM median (cross-check, weight 0.1). NFLX itself trades at 17.1x FY2027 consensus after hours.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. The discount is argued to persist through the horizon on two measured facts: lower forward EPS growth than the ad/platform peers (NFLX FY2028/FY2027 consensus 4.52/3.80 = +19% vs META +23.5%, AMZN +32.7%), and engagement-share loss (Nielsen: Netflix US TV share 7.9% June 2026 vs 8.3% a year earlier; YouTube record 14.2% in July), now with a larger combined Paramount-WBD rival. Netflix's ~19% EPS growth vs DIS ~8% argues against the low end (DIS 15.2x, FOXA 11.1x).

thesis_break_reason: $48 is ~12.6x FY2027 consensus EPS ($3.80), below even DIS (15.2x) and close to FOXA (11.1x), and ~4.5% under my engine bear value ($50.3). Trading there would most likely mean the base case broke: subscription growth falling to mid-single digits (price rises no longer sticking, churn rising against YouTube and the combined Paramount-WBD service), the margin path stalling near 33%, or the January 2027 guide implying revenue growth below 10%, not ordinary volatility (it is ~26% below the $64.85 effective start, ~0.8 sigma at 37% vol, and below the bear case's centre). Lowered from $50 in round 1 because the bear value moved from $48.3 to $50.3 and the break sits just under it.

catalysts.event: Nielsen US Gauge (August/September data) and analyst target revisions after the Q3 print
Paramount Skydance's first results after closing WBD (2026-10-06): plans and timing for combining HBO Max and Paramount+, content licensing to third parties
NFL Thanksgiving Eve game; Christmas Day NFL doubleheader 2026-12-25 (live ad inventory, sign-ups)
Q4 2026 results and first full-year 2027 guidance (revenue growth, margin, ad revenue)
First annual engagement report (semiannual reporting dropped): per-member hours are the bear debate
Ad tier launches in nine EMEA countries plus Colombia, Peru and New Zealand (first of 15 new markets)
2027 upfront ad commitments (2026 upfront nearly doubled commitments)
FIFA Women's World Cup on Netflix in the US and Canada
Q3 2027 results, around the horizon date

key_uncertainties: Engagement: whether per-member viewing stabilises against YouTube (Nielsen TV-share data, the annual engagement report) or keeps eroding (Wells Fargo: per-member hours ~8% below 2023).
Ad execution: 2026 cut to ~$2.7B; the 2027 path depends on ad-tech rollout and the 15-country expansion.
Pricing power: the March 2026 US increase drew loud Reddit/X backlash but management reports churn improved year on year; the next price round is the test.
Margin path after the October 2026 layoffs (~1,000 roles) versus sports-rights and content cost inflation.
Multiple: the stock rerated from ~35x to ~17x forward in a year; whether that stabilises depends on the engagement narrative more than on earnings.

Competition from the combined Paramount-WBD (merger completed 2026-10-06; ~200M DTC subs across HBO Max and Paramount+ to be merged into one platform): content bidding, licensed-title pulls and bundling.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine says the 18x P/E / 14x EV/EBITDA horizon multiples imply an 8.8% WACC on this driver set (vs 9.2% used, built on the 5.12% 10y), i.e. at 9.2% they require slightly more than the modelled path: revenue growth fading from ~10.6% (2027) to ~6.6% (2030) then 3% forever, with GAAP EBIT margin reaching 36%. That is plausible but not conservative given the long-dated risks (YouTube's record 14.2% TV share, the combined Paramount-WBD rival, sports-rights inflation), which is why the margin was trimmed from 37.5% to 36% and no premium multiple is used. Today's $64.85 at 17.1x FY2027 consensus implies roughly the same path with margins stalling ~1.5-2pt lower, or a ~9.8% WACC.

reasoning: Round 2. Start: $68.69 close, $64.85 after hours following Q3 2026 (EPS $0.87 beat, revenue $12.87B, 34.6% margin) with the 2026 ad outlook cut to ~$2.7B, FY revenue $51.1B and FCF ~$12B. Supervisor findings acted on, each re-checked at source: (1) risk-free: the Treasury curve shows the 10y at 5.12% on 2026-10-20 (my 4.3% was the bill rate); I rebuilt the cost of equity with my own 3y weekly beta vs SPY (1.04; 2y 0.92, 5y 1.43) and Damodaran's 2026-10-01 implied ERP of 4.20% (replacing a 5.0% judgment), giving a 9.2% WACC, below the supervisor's 9.4% because the sourced ERP is lower than my old judgment; (2) FY2030 margin trimmed from 37.5% to 36.0% with a scaled-peer bracket (DIS ~24% vs META ~48% TTM EBITDA margin) and live-sports and Paramount-WBD cost pressure; (3) tax cut from 17% (TTM, inflated by the WBD fee) to a normalised 15.5%; (4) EV/EBITDA weight cut from 0.3 to 0.1 and P/E raised to 0.7; (5) Paramount-WBD and M&A risks added. New fact the supervisor did not have: the Paramount-WBD merger completed on 2026-10-06 (WBD S-8 POS; Form 15 deregistration 2026-10-16), so this risk is now live, not contingent on the state AG suit; I trimmed FY2027 UCAN growth from 8% to 7%. No credible ad-margin estimate exists, so ads keep the company margin. Alternative-lane evidence (round 1, unchanged) is mixed-to-negative on engagement: Nielsen US TV share 7.9% June 2026 vs 8.3%, YouTube records (14.2% July); Netflix H1 hours +~2%; Wells Fargo per-member hours ~8% below 2023; offsets: Poland share rising, Sensor Tower GTA VI download spike, Antenna cord-cutter plan choice, WARC CTV ad share to ~9% by 2027, management-reported churn improvement. The Reddit/X backlash stays out of the numbers. No round-2 search found a verifiable post-price-rise Antenna churn figure (Puck paywalled). Valuation: DCF $69.7 (w 0.2), 18x NTM P/E $76.0 (w 0.7), 14x EV/EBITDA $71.2 (w 0.1) => $74.25 (round 1 $73.62): lower margin and the higher risk-free are offset by the lower sourced ERP, lower tax and the reweighting toward the P/E leg. Model FY2027 EPS ~$3.79 vs $3.80 consensus. Scenarios $50.3/$74.3/$93.5 at 25/50/25. Ladder: the engine distribution (median $73.6) gets ~1/3 weight against a lognormal from the $64.85 effective start at ~37% vol, median ~$68.5, P(>= $69) 0.485; left tail kept fatter than the scenario mixture (P(< $48) ~17.5%) because the stock de-rated 40%+ in a year on narrative. Lane share dipped to 12 of 22 sources because the corrections needed primary data (Treasury, prices, filings).
